criteria.text: The response concludes that the Quality Agreement defines Customer Germplasm more narrowly than the MSA, so that DNA extracts and derived genotypic/marker data carry no segregation, chain-of-custody or return/destruction obligation on Dronusk. It identifies where this arises (Quality Agreement Section 1.2 or Section 6, or MSA Section 1, 2.3 or 7.4), explains why this matters to Tanair, and recommends a fix.
hints: living plant tissue physically delivered by Customer

criteria.text: The response concludes that the Permitted Assignee exception lets Dronusk assign the MSA, along with custody of Tanair's germplasm and data, to any acquirer of its lab business, including a Tanair competitor, without Tanair's consent. It identifies where this arises (MSA Section 15.2 or the Section 1 definition of Permitted Assignee), explains why this matters to Tanair, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Order Form No. 1's own liability cap, which equals the total Order Form Fees ($186,400) and has no exclusions, displaces the MSA Section 11.3 uncapped carve-outs for the season's work. As a result, germplasm loss or misappropriation, confidentiality breaches and indemnified claims are capped. The response identifies where this arises (Order Form No. 1 Section 6, or MSA Section 2.3 or 11.3), explains why this matters to Tanair, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the parent-level merger with Kelbrin Agronomics described in Tanair's October 5, 2026 letter is a Change of Control under the MSA. Because Dronusk's prior written consent has not been sought or obtained, Dronusk could terminate the MSA and all Order Forms on 30 days' notice after closing. The response identifies where this arises (MSA Section 14.3 or the Section 1 Change of Control definition, or the October 5, 2026 letter), explains why this matters to Tanair, and recommends a fix.

The response states that under the MSA's order of precedence (Section 2.3), the MSA body is subordinate to the other contract documents, so the Quality Agreement and/or Order Forms prevail over the MSA body in a conflict.
The response is a memo addressed to the supervising partner. For each issue it sets out the location (document and section), why the issue matters to Tanair, and a recommended fix.
The response prioritises the issues or flags which issue(s) need the partner's attention first.
The response claims that Tanair's October 5, 2026 letter requested or obtained Dronusk's consent to the change of control.
